newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: INTERVIEW - Avonmore says set for growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Avonmore says set for growth in 97.

text.p: Irish food group Avonmore Foods Plc said on Monday it was well positioned for further growth in 1997, particularly in the UK dairy and meat division and the U.S. cheese and food ingredients business.

"We are well resourced and we are confident of further growth," group secretary Brendan Graham told Reuters after the group reported a 13.7 percent rise in 1996/7 pre-tax profits to 36.45 million Irish pounds.
He said the group's world-wide milk pool increased by five percent to almost 500 million gallons during 1996 and the group was well set to top that in 1997.

Avonmore said its operations in Ireland, the UK, and the U.S. were firmly established and adapting well to changing circumstances, and said the group was confident of continuing profit and earnings growth in the current year.
The group said it was particularly pleased with its growth potential in the United States and Britain.

"Growth opportunities in the UK dairy and meat sectors and in the U.S. cheese and food ingredients market are being followed up," Avonmore said, noting that turnover from the group's U.S. operations increased by 27% to 218 million Irish pounds during 1996.
"Avonmore West is very strong performer and very well positioned in the U.S.," Graham said.

He said the U.S. division has consolidated its position as the largest north-west U.S. cheese and whey-based food ingredients manufacturer and the group's presence will be further boosted by a $20 million capital investment plan, to be completed by mid-1997.
Avonmore expects its U.S. operations to produce 100,000 tonnes of the group's total cheese output of 145,000 tonnes in 1997.

Avonmore Dairies, the fifth largest liquid milk supplier in England and Wales, increased its share of the UK liquid milk market primarily through the growth of sales to retail multiples, the group said.
Graham predicts further sales and margin growth as UK milk costs reduce. This should underpin continuing margin improvement, he said.
Avonmore said its UK meats business also had an excellent year with turnover up to 136 million punts from 123 million.

In Ireland the company's milk products division was impacted from early in the year by the fall in world dairy product prices but maintained buoyancy by "switching operations to higher margin products".
The consumer products division consolidated its liquid milk market share and improved cheese sales, also recording strong growth in sales of convenience foods, particularly soups, it said.

The BSE crisis had limited impact on its business, Graham said, as its beef operations account for only seven percent of group turnover at this stage. It said consumption levels have shown some recovery in early 1997 however.
Partly as a consequence of the BSE crisis, there was strong demand for sheepmeat and increased sales of fresh consumer meats resulted in investment in value added facilities, Avonmore said.
Further sales growth is expected in Irish and European markets in 1997.
